# Inphinit Framework Documentation

> Inphinit is a lightweight, high-performance PHP micro-framework designed to leverage native PHP functions and use a concise structure for processing route callbacks while consuming minimal server resources.

## Essential

- [Getting Started](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/): Introduces the framework and provides instructions for installing it using Composer or Git.
- [Checkup](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/checkup.html): Provides instructions for using Checkup to help assess the health of server requirements and suggest ideal configurations.
- [Configurations](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/configurations.html): Explains different configuration approaches adapted to different purposes, including the use of environment variables.
- [Structure](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/structure.html): Introduces the basic structure of an application using the framework, explaining each file and directory.
- [Events](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/events.html): Explains how the framework's event system works, providing a decoupled way to transmit data without the need to write complex structures.
- [Debugging](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/debugging.html): Introduces debugging mode, with integration with text editors and AI assistants to locate and assess the causes of errors that occur.
- [Maintenance](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/maintenance.html): Introduces maintenance mode, explaining how to enable and disable it and how to bypass it under specific conditions.

## Web Application

- [Routing](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/): Explains how to create routes in the web context based on the HTTP verb and URL path, also allowing routes to be grouped by scope (domain, subdomain, or URL path).
- [Controllers](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/controllers.html): Introduces and explains how controllers are used in the web context to centralize route logic.
- [Implicit Route Controllers](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/implicit-route-controllers.html): Explains how to create routes based on the methods of a controller class, following naming conventions.
- [Resource Routes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/resource.html): Explains how to create RESTful routes based on the methods of a controller class.
- [Sendfile](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/production/sendfile.html): Explains how to use `X-Accel-Redirect` and `X-Sendfile` in the application.
- [Error Pages](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/error-pages.html): Explains how to handle error codes coming from the SAPI: maintenance mode (503), undefined route (404), or HTTP method not allowed (405).
- [Session](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/session.html): Explains how to use the file-based session system, which avoids blocking the entire request unlike PHP's native session system.
- [Views](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/views.html): Explains how to use views in the Web context.

## HTTP Utilities

- [HTTP Request](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/request.html): Introduces methods for analyzing the HTTP request.
- [HTTP Response](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/response.html): Introduces methods for manipulating the HTTP response, such as headers, caching, and forcing downloads using `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
- [HTTP Response Codes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/response-codes.html): Contains a list of HTTP codes as constants, which can be used to avoid magic numbers and also obtain the corresponding message for a received code as a string.
- [HTTP Content Negotiation](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/content-negotiation.html): Explains how to adapt the response in the Web context according to the request through headers such as `Accept` and similar headers.
- [Cookies](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/http-cookies.html): Introduces a cookie manager based on cookie jars that isolates cookies in different contexts through prefixes.
- [Experimental HTTP Resources](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/http-resources.html): Introduces HTTP utilities that are still experimental but may already be useful, such as overriding the HTTP method using fields such as `_method=` or headers such as `x-http-method`.

## Console

- [Console Commands](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/console-commands.html): Explains how to create commands for the console in the CLI context.
- [Task Scheduling](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/task-scheduling.html): Explains how to schedule functions, internal commands, and even shell commands for execution at specific minutes, hours, or days, with support for recurring intervals and one-time execution at a future date.

## Web Servers

- [Apache](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/apache.html): Explains how to configure Apache for use with the application in the Web context.
- [Caddy & FrankenPHP](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/caddy-frankenphp.html): Explains how to configure Caddy and FrankenPHP for use with the application in the Web context.
- [IIS](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/iis.html): Explains how to configure IIS with PHP for use with the application in the Web context.
- [IIS Express](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/iis-express.html): Explains how to configure IIS Express with PHP for use with the application in the Web context.
- [Nginx](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/nginx.html): Explains how to configure Nginx for use with the application in the Web context.

## DOM

- [DOM, XML, HTML](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/): Explains how to parse HTML and XML documents and strings, and can also be used for simple web crawlers.
- [CSS Selectors in PHP](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/css-selector.html): Explains how to find elements in an HTML or XML document or string using CSS selectors on the server side, generally a simpler alternative to XPath.
- [DOM with Arrays](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/dom-with-arrays.html): Explains how to convert HTML and XML to arrays, and vice versa, which can be useful for converting between different formats.
- [DOM Errors](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/errors.html): Explains how the debugger can analyze errors in documents, locating the source of failures in the document structure.

## Utilities

- [Utilities](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/): Introduces common utilities for strings and arrays that simplify certain operations.
- [URL Utilities](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/url.html): Explains how to use the utility to parse and normalize URLs, including slug generation.
- [Version Utilities](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/version.html): Explains how to use the utility to parse a version string based on Semantic Versioning, allowing two different versions to be compared or `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` values to be adjusted in a simplified way.

## Experimental Utilities

- [Experimental](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/): Introduces experimental utilities being considered for inclusion in the framework in future releases, but which can already be used.
- [Markdown](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/markdown.html): Introduces the utility for converting Markdown documents to HTML, allowing customization of the generated HTML elements.
- [CSV/TSV Reader](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/csv-tsv-reader.html): Introduces the utility for reading CSV and TSV documents in a straightforward way, allowing the content to be converted to other formats or to a DTO.

## Packages

- [Inphinit Proxy](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/packages/inphinit-proxy.html): Inphinit Proxy is a proxy library intended for use with html2canvas or similar client-side tools that need to bypass CORS restrictions.
